page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-96 is a memory-dense compute instance driven by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 744 GB, yielding approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, complemented by 260 MB of Level 3 cache and hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. The configuration includes zero integrated GPUs and does not supply local storage, requiring external persistent disks for storage operations.

Performance assessments reflect high parallel computing capability and strong data handling speeds. The platform achieved a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21,073, supported by an uncached large-block read memory bandwidth of 288.74 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 124.06 GB/sec. Hardware-assisted cryptographic and vector processing capabilities yield high throughput in data security benchmarks and static web serving, which reached 128.55 GB/sec. In-memory operations demonstrate notable efficiency, with Redis SET benchmarks recording 106.15 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a resource profile tailored for RAM-bound applications without the cost overhead of dedicated graphics hardware. The absence of local solid-state drives necessitates planning around network storage throughput for I/O-intensive workloads. Given the substantial RAM allocation and high-throughput multi-threaded CPU execution, the c4-highmem-96 is suited for large in-memory databases, distributed cache clusters, big data analytics pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
